channel.title: Financial Regulation Hub
channel.description: New and amended financial regulation for NBFCs, HFCs and other regulated entities, across all sections.

item.title: SEBI: Simplification of client on-boarding and rationalisation of risk management framework at KYC Registration Agencies
item.description:
SEBI · Circular

Effective 2026-12-24.

Who it covers: All SEBI-registered intermediaries that on-board clients, and KYC Registration Agencies.

  • Common supplementary client information (such as income range, FATCA/CRS details, PEP status and occupation) is centralised at the KRA, along with CKYC ID, DIGIPIN and the expiry date of the officially valid document.
  • Intermediaries upload the specified KYC information to the KRA within three working days of completing KYC.
  • In force from 24-12-2026; KRAs issue an operating procedure within 30 days.

Official source

item.title: IRDAI: Constitution of the Fund Management Committee under the IRDAI (Policyholders' Education and Protection Fund) Regulations, 2026
item.description:
IRDAI · Order · IRDAI/PP&GR/ORD/MISC/155/11/2026

Effective 2026-11-25.

Who it covers: IRDAI; administration of the Policyholders' Education and Protection Fund.

  • Sets up the committee that manages the Fund under regulation 7(2).
  • Members serve two years, extendable by two more.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: All IFSC entities to act on CERT-In advisories and vulnerability notes
item.description:
IFSC · Circular · IFSCA circular dated 25-11-2026

Effective 2026-11-25.

Who it covers: All regulated entities, including systems run for them by the parent or third parties.

  • Comply with CERT-In advisories and vulnerability notes, including for systems run by the parent or vendors.
  • Set up a tracking mechanism within 30 days; assessment and patching duties apply to advisories issued from 25-11-2026.
  • Reminds entities that CERT-In's own directions (6-hour incident reporting, 180-day logs) apply independently.

Official source

item.title: IRDAI: Two study groups on transparency and accountability in health insurance claims
item.description:
IRDAI · Press release

Who it covers: Health insurers and general insurers writing health business.

  • The IAC Sub-Committee on Health Insurance has formed two study groups: one on claims and grievance metrics and standard reason codes for rejections and deductions, the other on real-time tracking of the claim journey.
  • Both are to report by 26-12-2026. No rule has changed yet.

Official source

item.title: RBI: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026
item.description:
RBI · Amendment Directions · RBI/2026-27/306; DOR.STR.REC.258/21-04-177/2026-27

Effective 2027-04-01.

Who it covers: NBFCs covered by para 3 of the NBFC Securitisation Transactions Directions 2025: NBFC-D, NBFC-ICC, NBFC-Factor, NBFC-MFI, NBFC-IFC, IDF-NBFC and HFCs (para 3(vii)), all layers. Outside para 3: CICs, MGCs, NBFC-P2P, NBFC-AA, NOFHCs, SPDs and Type I NBFCs, so an Upper Layer CIC is not covered as originator. Direct assignments of loans fall under the separate Transfer of Loan Exposures Directions and are not affected. The same changes were made on the same day for commercial banks, SFBs and AIFIs (RBI/2026-27/304, 305, 307).

  • para 26 (substituted): the issuance, holding and subsequent transfer of securitisation notes must be in dematerialised form only. The ₹1 crore minimum ticket size applies at issue and at every later transfer. The originator must ensure that its agreement with the SPE requires the SPE to put in place arrangements with entities such as the registrar, depository and stock exchange, "as may be applicable", to secure the minimum ticket size. Proviso: notes with amortisation structures may be traded at amortised value if the ticket size falls below ₹1 crore. Explanation: ticket size is the investment of a single investor.
  • para 27 (substituted): for an offer of securitisation notes to the public, Regulation 21 of the SEBI (Issue and Listing of Securitised Debt Instruments and Security Receipts) Regulations 2008 must be complied with. RBI's own earlier wording (listing "recommended, though not mandatory"; offers to fifty or more persons to be listed) is removed, so the SEBI Regulations now decide what is a public offer.
  • para 27A (new): transactions in notes issued before 01-04-2027 must also comply with paras 26 and 27. There is no grandfathering for older notes.
  • Effective 01-04-2027 (para 3). Press release 2026-2027/1550 says this finalises the draft of 27-07-2026 after comments.

Official source

item.title: RBI: Governor meets MDs and CEOs of select NBFCs, HFCs and industry bodies
item.description:
RBI · Meeting (press release) · Press Release 2026-2027/1554

Who it covers: Select NBFCs (including Government NBFCs), HFCs and MFIs. Sa-Dhan, MFIN and FIDC took part, and the NHB MD & CEO attended. No new directions were issued.

  • The Governor stressed responsible and sustainable credit growth, fair recovery practices, use of CKYCR for onboarding, and a comprehensive, risk-based approach to cyber and IT risk.

Official source

item.title: RBI: Draft Amendment Directions on 'Preventive Safeguards for Electronic Banking Transactions (EBTs)'
item.description:
RBI · Draft Amendment Directions (for comment) · Press Release 2026-2027/1548

Who it covers: Seven drafts amending the Responsible Business Conduct Directions for commercial banks, SFBs, payments banks, LABs, RRBs, UCBs and RCBs. No NBFC or HFC draft. Comments due by 14-12-2026.

  • Seven draft amendments to the banks' Responsible Business Conduct Directions. Per the press release, they aim to give customers greater control over how and how far their digital payment channels can be used, and to widen the definition of "negligence by a bank" in the 24-06-2026 customer-liability amendment.
  • The press release does not describe the detailed proposals; they are in the seven draft PDFs, which were not read here.

Official source

item.title: IRDAI: Re-constitution of the Advisory Committee to review the performance of the Insurance Ombudsman system
item.description:
IRDAI · Order · IRDAI/PP&GR/ORD/MISC/154/11/2026

Effective 2026-11-23.

Who it covers: IRDAI and the Insurance Ombudsman system.

  • Re-constitutes the committee under rule 19(1) of the Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 for two years.
  • It meets at least twice a year and reports every year.

Official source

item.title: IRDAI: Expert Committee to examine responses to the consultation paper on Recalibrating Economics of Insurance Distribution
item.description:
IRDAI · Order · IRDAI/INT/ORD/MISC/157/11/2026

Effective 2026-11-23.

Who it covers: Insurers and all distribution channels.

  • Sets up an expert committee to review the responses (about 2.18 lakh answers from over 13,000 respondents) to the 23-09-2026 consultation paper and recommend refinements.
  • No rule has changed yet.

Official source

item.title: RBI: RBI imposes monetary penalty on an NBFC
item.description:
RBI · Enforcement (press release) · Press Release 2026-2027/1537 (order dated 17-11-2026)

Who it covers: Another lender (described as an NBFC in secondary sources). It is a routine enforcement order and creates no new rule.

  • Penalty of ₹7.50 lakh by order of 17-11-2026, under RBI Act s.58G(1)(b) read with s.58B(5)(aa), following a statutory inspection of the position as on 31-03-2026.
  • Findings: the company failed to obtain PAN (or its e-document) or Form 60 when establishing account-based relationships, and failed to escalate partly or wholly rejected complaints to the Internal Ombudsman within the prescribed time. RBI cites its KYC and Internal Ombudsman directions without paragraph numbers.

Official source

item.title: IRDAI: Penalty on a standalone health insurer for claim repudiations and deductions
item.description:
IRDAI · Enforcement order (penalty) · IRDAI/E&C/ORD/MISC/153/11/2026

Effective 2026-11-20.

Who it covers: The health insurer named in the order. The rules applied are unchanged.

  • Rs 2 crore penalty under s. 102 of the Insurance Act for repudiating claims on untenable grounds and making deductions not supported by policy terms.
  • Breaches found of regulations 27(v) and 33(d) of the Health Insurance Regulations 2016 and regulation 21(3) of the TPA Regulations; warnings and directions also issued.

Official source

item.title: DPDP: Consent Manager registration opens under the DPDP Act
item.description:
DPDP · Commencement · s. 6(9) and s. 27(1)(d) of the Act; rule 4 of the DPDP Rules, 2025

Effective 2026-11-13.

Who it covers: Companies that want to register as Consent Managers, and Data Fiduciaries that plan to accept consent through them.

  • Rule 4 and the First Schedule apply from 13-11-2026: an Indian company with net worth of at least Rs 2 crore and an independently certified platform may apply to the Board.
  • The Board may inquire into a breach of a Consent Manager's registration conditions (s. 27(1)(d)).
  • The duties of Data Fiduciaries on notice, consent, security and breaches still start on 13-05-2027.

Official source

item.title: NHB: Arbitrators must be independent; report action to NHB
item.description:
NHB · Advisory · RBI DoR.CO.BCG(MCS).No.S6464/01.01.008/2026-27

Effective 2026-11-12.

Who it covers: Banks and NBFCs, including HFCs.

  • After a Delhi High Court order of 30-09-2026, RBI cautioned lenders against appointing the same arbitrators unilaterally across many disputes.
  • Arbitrators are to be appointed only in line with the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 and court rulings on independence and neutrality.
  • HFCs report the action taken to NHB.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: FATCA and CRS reporting revised under the Income-Tax Act, 2025 and Income-Tax Rules, 2026
item.description:
SEBI · Circular

Effective 2026-11-11.

Who it covers: Registered intermediaries that are Reporting Financial Institutions.

  • Reporting and due diligence now follow s. 508 of the Income-Tax Act, 2025 and rules 238 to 240 and Form 166 of the Income-Tax Rules, 2026.
  • Self-certification, controlling person and account classification systems must capture the new fields; FATCA/CRS certifications are uploaded to the KRA.

Official source

item.title: IRDAI: Working Groups on convergence of the Risk Based Capital framework with Ind AS
item.description:
IRDAI · Order · IRDAI/RBC/ORD/MISC/150/11/2026

Effective 2026-11-10.

Who it covers: All insurers.

  • Sets up Life and Non-Life working groups so that Ind AS financial statements become the starting point for RBC, with defined prudential adjustments.
  • No rule has changed yet.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: SEBI (Settlement of Administrative and Civil Proceedings) Regulations, 2026 in force
item.description:
SEBI · Regulations · SEBI/LAD-DOP/2026/318

Effective 2026-11-07.

Who it covers: Anyone facing or likely to face SEBI proceedings.

  • Replace the Settlement Proceedings Regulations, 2018.
  • Settlement notices before a show cause notice, a formula-based settlement amount, and fast track settlement for delayed or wrong-format disclosures.
  • Applications within 90 days of a show cause notice; pending cases not settled under the 2018 rules may apply within 90 days at a 20% higher amount.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Consultation paper: AML/CFT certification for Principal Officers of intermediaries
item.description:
SEBI · Consultation paper

Who it covers: All intermediaries registered under s. 12 of the SEBI Act.

  • Proposes a mandatory AML/CFT certification for the Principal Officer responsible for PMLA compliance.
  • No rule has changed yet.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Framework for net settlement of funds for mutual fund cash market transactions
item.description:
SEBI · Circular

Effective 2027-04-01.

Who it covers: Mutual funds, custodians, stock brokers and clearing corporations.

  • Funds for outright transactions in the cash segment may be settled net at the level of each scheme; securities still settle gross.
  • No netting across schemes. In force from 01-04-2027.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Review of the framework for Accredited Investors
item.description:
SEBI · Circular

Effective 2026-11-05.

Who it covers: AIF managers, SIF AMCs and portfolio managers, and their investors.

  • Managers may determine and record an investor's accredited status themselves, valid for three years and recognised across the same group.
  • Securities market exposure qualifies: at least Rs 5 crore for individuals, HUFs, family trusts and sole proprietorships, and Rs 20 crore for bodies corporate and other trusts.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Review of KYC process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
item.description:
SEBI · Circular

Effective 2026-12-03.

Who it covers: Intermediaries on-boarding NRI, OCI and foreign national individual clients.

  • Digital KYC is allowed for individual clients located in FATF-compliant countries, without being in India.
  • Intermediaries may rely on KYC by another SEBI or financial sector regulated entity through KRA or CKYCRR records.

Official source

item.title: IRDAI: Exposure Draft: IRDAI (Subsidiary Instructions and Consultative Committees) Regulations, 2026
item.description:
IRDAI · Exposure draft (for comment)

Who it covers: All regulated entities.

  • Proposes regulations under the new ss. 114B and 114C of the Insurance Act (inserted by the SBSR Act 2025) on the scope of subsidiary instructions, consultation, urgent instructions, review and withdrawal, and Consultative Committees.
  • Comments were due by 23-11-2026.

Official source

item.title: IRDAI: Master Circular on Registration, Capital Structure, Transfer of Shares and Amalgamation of Insurers, 2026
item.description:
IRDAI · Master Circular · IRDAI/F&I/CIR/MISC/142/11/2026

Effective 2026-11-02.

Who it covers: Applicants for registration and registered insurers.

  • Consolidates procedure, forms and documents under the Registration Regulations as amended on 31-07-2026.
  • Replaces the 2024 Master Circular on the same subject.

Official source

item.title: IRDAI: Four Layer Structure: Motor Insurance Policy
item.description:
IRDAI · Circular · IRDAI/NL/CIR/MISC/145/11/2026

Who it covers: General insurers selling private car and two-wheeler policies, and their distributors.

  • Uniform wordings and an option form for a four-layer motor policy: third-party liability (mandatory), occupant liability (optional), personal accident and own damage.
  • A Customer Information Sheet is mandatory. Issued after the Supreme Court's order in CA 14369/2025.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Extension of timeline for digital accessibility compliance
item.description:
SEBI · Circular

Effective 2026-10-30.

Who it covers: All SEBI regulated entities.

  • Appointment of an accessibility auditor, the accessibility audit of digital platforms and fixing its findings are extended to 31-01-2027.

Official source

item.title: IBC: Real estate CIRPs: RERA compliance, RERA's views on plans and site notices
item.description:
IBC · Circular · IBBI/CIRP/110/2026

Effective 2026-10-30.

Who it covers: IRPs and RPs of corporate debtors with real estate projects, CoCs and prospective resolution applicants.

  • RPs must comply with RERA during the CIRP.
  • RPs may invite RERA's written views on plans and share them with the CoC and bidders.
  • The CIRP must be shown on signboards at each project site and office within 7 days of appointment.

Official source

item.title: IBC: Revised Form CA with a separate part for homebuyers
item.description:
IBC · Circular · IBBI/CIRP/109/2026

Effective 2026-10-30.

Who it covers: Financial creditors in a class, including real estate allottees, and IRPs and RPs.

  • Form CA has Part I for other creditors in a class and Part II for allottees.
  • Claims filed earlier need not be refiled.

Official source

item.title: IBC: CIRP Regulations amended (fifth amendment of 2026)
item.description:
IBC · Regulation · IBBI (Insolvency Resolution Process for Corporate Persons) (Fifth Amendment) Regulations, 2026

Effective 2026-10-30.

Who it covers: Everyone in a CIRP.

  • The CIRP Regulations were amended again; the consolidated text as on 30-10-2026 is the current version.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Further extension for debenture trustees to move non-SEBI activities to separate business units
item.description:
SEBI · Circular

Effective 2026-10-27.

Who it covers: Debenture trustees.

  • The deadline to comply with regulation 9C and the separate business unit framework moves to 27-04-2027 while an expert group reviews it.

Official source

item.title: FEMA: Compounding of certain FEMA contraventions delegated to RBI Regional Offices
item.description:
FEMA · Circular · A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 28/2026-27

Effective 2026-10-23.

Who it covers: Applicants compounding contraventions of the Borrowing and Lending Regulations, the Guarantees Regulations or the overseas investment framework.

  • Borrowing and lending, and guarantee, contraventions are compounded by the Regional Office with jurisdiction over the applicant's registered office.
  • Overseas investment cases go to one of seven Regional Offices by the prefix of the unique identification number; mixed cases stay with the Central Office.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: Further issues: one lead exchange handles queries for both NSE and BSE
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange circular · NSE/CML/2026/22

Effective 2026-11-01.

Who it covers: Listed companies applying for in-principle approval of a further issue of shares.

  • Applications are still filed with every exchange, but the exchanges assign a lead exchange in turn.
  • The other exchange routes its queries through the lead exchange; the company answers only the lead exchange.
  • Applies to applications filed on or after 01-11-2026.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: RFQ trades in corporate bonds settle on T+0 until 5 p.m.
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange circular · NSE/DS/76973; BSE notice 20261019-21

Effective 2026-10-19.

Who it covers: Participants on the NSE and BSE RFQ platforms.

  • RFQ trading hours for T+0 settlement extended to 5 p.m. (NSE from 19-10-2026; BSE from 21-10-2026).
  • Participants must confirm their entity type every half-year to keep platform access.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Closing Auction Session, market timings and settlement methodology for derivatives
item.description:
SEBI · Circular

Effective 2026-12-07.

Who it covers: Stock exchanges, clearing corporations and stock brokers.

  • Changes to the closing auction session, market timings and the settlement price method for derivatives; parts take effect from 07-12-2026.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026
item.description:
SEBI · Amendment Regulations · SEBI/LAD-DOP/2026/329

Effective 2026-10-14.

Who it covers: Entities that list non-convertible debt securities.

  • Regulation 62A(1) substituted: an entity whose non-convertible debt securities are listed on or after 14-10-2026 must list all non-convertible debt securities it issues after that listing.
  • Regulation 62A(2) and (3) omitted.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026
item.description:
SEBI · Amendment Regulations · SEBI/LAD-NRO/GN/2026/326

Effective 2026-10-14.

Who it covers: AIFs, their managers and investors.

  • Accredited investors may now be accredited by a specified SEBI-registered entity, and securities market exposure becomes a qualifying test.
  • Regulation 25 on dispute resolution between investors and the AIF or manager is substituted.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Consultation paper: review of ICDR provisions on SME IPOs
item.description:
SEBI · Consultation paper

Who it covers: SME issuers and merchant bankers.

  • Working group recommendations to revise the SME IPO framework.
  • No rule has changed yet.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Consultation paper: monitoring and disclosure of utilisation of issue proceeds (LODR review)
item.description:
SEBI · Consultation paper

Who it covers: Listed entities raising funds.

  • Working group recommendations on monitoring agency reports and disclosure of how issue proceeds are used.
  • No rule has changed yet.

Official source

item.title: FEMA: Non-deliverable rupee derivatives for non-residents only for hedging; reserve on AD banks' own hedges
item.description:
FEMA · Circular · A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 27/2026-27

Effective 2026-10-12.

Who it covers: AD banks with IFSC banking units, standalone primary dealers, and non-resident users.

  • AD banks may offer non-deliverable rupee derivatives to non-residents only for hedging.
  • A 20% Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve applies to AD banks' own rupee hedges where they buy foreign currency.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: Newly debt-listed entities must list all later NCDs
item.description:
Exchanges · SEBI regulation · SEBI/LAD-DOP/2026/329 (LODR Third Amendment)

Effective 2026-10-14.

Who it covers: Entities whose non-convertible debt securities are listed on or after 14-10-2026.

  • Reg 62A(1) substituted: an entity whose NCDs are listed on or after the amendment's Gazette publication (14-10-2026) must list all non-convertible debt securities it issues after that listing.
  • Reg 62A(2) and (3) omitted.

Official source

item.title: FEMA: No rebooking of cancelled rupee derivatives; threshold without proof of exposure cut to USD 5 million
item.description:
FEMA · Circular · A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 25/2026-27

Effective 2026-10-10.

Who it covers: Users hedging with AD banks, including ECB and trade credit borrowers, and AD banks.

  • Cancelled rupee derivatives may not be rebooked; rollovers on maturity are still allowed.
  • Positions without establishing the underlying exposure fall from USD 100 million to USD 5 million.
  • Users give an undertaking that the same exposure is not hedged with another AD bank.

Official source

item.title: FEMA: Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve of 20% on rupee derivatives hedging current account payments
item.description:
FEMA · Circular · A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 26/2026-27

Effective 2026-10-10.

Who it covers: AD banks and users buying foreign currency forward against rupees for current account transactions.

  • AD banks keep 20% of the rupee notional of each such contract above USD 2 million as cash with RBI until the contract ends.
  • Splitting deals to stay below the threshold is a violation.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: SEBI (Intermediaries) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2026: common advertisement code
item.description:
SEBI · Amendment Regulations · SEBI/LAD-NRO/GN/2026/323

Who it covers: Regulated entities that advertise, including AMCs, stock brokers and AIF managers.

  • New Chapter IIID sets a common advertisement code, including rules on celebrity endorsements and influencers.
  • In force 180 days after publication on 09-10-2026. The MF Regulations' own advertisement schedule is removed by a matching amendment.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2026
item.description:
SEBI · Regulations

Effective 2027-04-01.

Who it covers: Portfolio managers, including AMCs that offer portfolio management services.

  • New regulations replace the Portfolio Managers Regulations, 2020 from 01-04-2027.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: Credit Risk-o-Meter on debt offer documents and bond platforms
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange circular · NSE circular of 08-10-2026; BSE notice 20261008-23

Effective 2026-11-21.

Who it covers: Debt issuers, arrangers and online bond platform providers.

  • Offer documents, placement memoranda, advertisements and online bond platforms must show a Credit Risk-o-Meter.
  • The rating agency, the rating and, for unsecured debt, the word 'unsecured' in bold red appear below it.
  • In force 45 days after 07-10-2026.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: Rs 10,000 NCDs: some regulated, listed issuers need no merchant banker
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange circular · NSE/CML/D/2026/06; BSE notice 20261008-22

Effective 2026-10-07.

Who it covers: Issuers regulated by SEBI, RBI, IRDAI or PFRDA, including NBFCs and HFCs.

  • For private placements at Rs 10,000 face value, no merchant banker is needed if the issuer is regulated by SEBI, RBI, IRDAI or PFRDA; has been listed for a year with no pending LODR fines; has had no default in the last three financial years and the current year (auditor's certificate); issues senior debt secured on its own identifiable assets; and is rated AA- or above on the placement date.

Official source

item.title: Exchanges: New caps on ISINs for privately placed debt
item.description:
Exchanges · Exchange circular · NSE/CML/D/2026/05; BSE notice 20261008-21

Effective 2026-10-07.

Who it covers: Issuers of privately placed debt securities and their arrangers.

  • Up to 17 ISINs may mature in a financial year: 12 for plain vanilla debt and 5 for structured, market-linked, floating rate, zero coupon and Tier II bonds, plus 6 for s. 54EC bonds.
  • Outstanding floating rate, zero coupon and Tier II ISINs issued before the circular are grandfathered.
  • One more plain vanilla ISIN for each Rs 3,000 crore once the amount maturing in the year reaches Rs 15,000 crore.
  • Government-serviced (EBR) bonds and ESG debt securities are outside the count.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: No mandatory merchant banker for certain private placements of debt by listed regulated issuers
item.description:
SEBI · Circular

Effective 2026-10-07.

Who it covers: Listed issuers regulated by SEBI, RBI, IRDAI or PFRDA issuing debt of Rs 10,000 face value on private placement.

  • Such issuers may skip the merchant banker if they meet all the conditions, including at least one year of listing and no pending fines.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: More ISINs for privately placed debt securities
item.description:
SEBI · Circular

Effective 2026-10-07.

Who it covers: Issuers of privately placed debt securities.

  • Up to 17 ISINs may mature in a financial year (12 plain vanilla, 5 structured and similar), plus six for capital gains bonds, with extra ISINs for large issuers.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Credit Risk-o-Meter for debt securities
item.description:
SEBI · Circular

Effective 2026-11-21.

Who it covers: Issuers of debt securities and online bond platform providers.

  • A colour-coded Credit Risk-o-Meter becomes mandatory in offer documents, abridged prospectuses, private placement memoranda, issuer advertisements and online bond platforms.
  • In force 45 days after issue.

Official source

item.title: DPDP: DPDP (Removal of Difficulties) Order, 2026 adjusts the wording of ss. 9(1) and 10(2)(c)(ii)
item.description:
DPDP · Order · S.O. 5458(E) dated 05-10-2026

Effective 2026-10-06.

Who it covers: Data Fiduciaries processing data of children or persons with disability, and Significant Data Fiduciaries.

  • s. 9(1) now refers to the personal data of a child or of a person with disability who has a lawful guardian.
  • s. 10(2)(c)(ii) now requires a periodic data audit.
  • No change to the commencement dates.

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Investor awareness messages on stock brokers' websites and apps (Project Jagrook)
item.description:
SEBI · Circular

Effective 2026-11-01.

Who it covers: Stock brokers.

  • From 01-11-2026, investor awareness messages shared by SEBI go on the landing page of brokers' websites, and alternate with risk disclosures on trading apps.

Official source

item.title: Other laws: Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 2026 in force: cloud and electronic bank records
item.description:
Other laws · Act · Act 15 of 2026

Effective 2026-10-01.

Who it covers: Banks, and other financial sector entities to which the Central Government extends the Act, producing account statements in court or tribunal.

  • The 1891 Act is repealed.
  • Bankers' books expressly include electronic, offsite, cloud and disaster-recovery records.
  • Certified copies can be signed digitally by the branch head, office head or an authorised officer, in the forms in the Schedules.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Deadline for FME certification courses extended to 31-12-2026
item.description:
IFSC · Circular · F. No. IFSCA-AIF/127/2026-Capital Markets/1

Effective 2026-09-29.

Who it covers: KMPs and specified employees of fund management entities.

  • KMPs and employees have until 31-12-2026 to complete the specified certification course (ICSI or ICAI).

Official source

item.title: SEBI: Master Circular for Debenture Trustees
item.description:
SEBI · Master Circular

Effective 2026-09-28.

Who it covers: Debenture trustees and issuers of listed debt.

  • Consolidates the circulars for debenture trustees.

Official source

item.title: NHB: Branch notice: insurance is voluntary and not linked to a loan
item.description:
NHB · Advisory · HO/DOS/DAK/2026/05646

Effective 2026-09-24.

Who it covers: All registered HFCs.
